subject: Storage zones that improve kitchen flow
hook: Is planning storage zones worth it in a small kitchen? Arguably, it matters more.
fb:
We often hear: 'Our kitchen is tiny, so zones are not really for us.' Usually, the opposite is true.

In a small or galley kitchen, the zones overlap, so a bit of order goes a long way. Bin and cleaning under the sink. Pans in the drawer nearest the hob. Everyday plates by the dishwasher. Food gathered into one tall unit rather than spread across three cupboards. And drawers instead of deep base cupboards, so nothing hides at the back.

gbp:
Is it worth planning storage zones in a small kitchen?

Yes, and arguably more than in a large one. In a small or galley kitchen the zones overlap, so the order of storage makes a bigger difference to how the room works day to day.

A few principles we use when designing compact bespoke kitchens:
- Keep the bin and cleaning products together at the sink
- Put pans and utensils in the drawer nearest the hob
- Store everyday plates and cutlery beside the dishwasher
- Gather food into one tall unit, such as a pull-out larder
- Use drawers rather than deep base cupboards, so nothing gets lost at the back

Every SUPERIO kitchen is made to measure in our own workshop, so we can use the awkward gaps that standard units leave behind. If you have a small kitchen in Stoke-on-Trent or nearby, book a free, no-obligation consultation and we will look at what your space can do.
